title: Albert Ammons and Indiana Avenue
summary: Palmer talks about Albert Ammons, working alternate weeks at the Indiana Avenue theater and when they met.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did you meet some boogie players? You know, I'm very interested in...

Yes. He's very fun of mine. Albert's a great fun of mine. I like his style very much. Albert Avenue was a great fun of mine. What do you mean? Uh... He's in fact, uh, he... he and I used to work at the Indiana Avenue Theater together, see, and he... Like, he'd take two weeks, three weeks. In which... Indiana Avenue. Indiana Avenue. Well, he'd play a few weeks and then I'd go in with my band. It was all donated like that. Did he have a band? Yeah. Yeah. Let me get ready. Just a minute. Oh, sure. He's a kid. Oh! The wheel. He used to... He's a tall, slim guy, black hair, much more than a young guy.
Now that's what my album piano player is. Yes. I can understand you. He plays... you still can play Marvel.
All right. I don't know... I have no... nothing to measure again. I don't know. I'm a person or something like that.
Yes. Talking about Albert Emmons, uh... When did you meet him first? Did you meet him in the 20s or later?

Oh, I met him in the 30s. In the 30s. Oh, yeah. Yeah. I met Albert... must have been around 34, 35. And he also had a band. Yeah. No, he was with Banks. He worked with a drummer by the name of Banks. Did you meet him with a drummer? Nah, he didn't ever have a band. I guess he did have a band later. I guess he did.
Yes, he once recorded with a band, Guy Kelly.
